articles.title: Why Shielded Defaults Matter
articles.description: Privacy works best when it is ordinary, understandable, and available by default.
articles.content:
# Why Shielded Defaults Matter

Financial privacy is the ability to choose what to reveal, when, and to whom. Zcash gives people tools for selective disclosure without making every transaction a public record.

## Better defaults, clearer choices

Good privacy tools should explain their tradeoffs plainly and keep people in control. A shielded default can reduce accidental exposure while preserving deliberate sharing.

articles.description: Addresses, confirmations, fees, and recovery explained without jargon.
articles.content:
# A Clear Guide to Zcash Wallets

A wallet helps you manage addresses, review transactions, and authorize sends. The most important habit is to understand how recovery works before relying on any wallet for meaningful value.

## Start carefully

Learn with small amounts, verify addresses, and keep recovery material offline and private.

articles.title: Selective Disclosure in Practice
articles.description: Share the information a situation needs without exposing an entire financial history.
articles.content:
# Selective Disclosure in Practice

Privacy and accountability are not opposites. Selective disclosure gives people a way to provide specific evidence without publishing unrelated activity.

## Context matters

Different relationships call for different levels of disclosure. Useful tools make those boundaries visible and understandable.

articles.title: Understanding Unified Addresses
articles.description: One address can describe several compatible ways to receive Zcash.
articles.content:
# Understanding Unified Addresses

A Unified Address can contain multiple receiver types. Compatible wallets choose the receiver they support while keeping the address presentation simple.

## Check compatibility

Before sending, confirm that both wallets support the intended receiver and network.

articles.title: How Light Clients Work
articles.description: A practical overview of compact blocks, scanning, and local wallet state.
articles.content:
# How Light Clients Work

Light clients use compact blockchain data to discover relevant transactions without downloading every full block. Wallet software scans that data and maintains local state.

## Verify progress

A useful wallet distinguishes synchronization progress from a current confirmed balance.

articles.title: Open Protocols and User Choice
articles.description: Interoperable foundations let people choose tools without giving up portability.
articles.content:
# Open Protocols and User Choice

Open protocols make it possible for independent tools to communicate. That creates room for experimentation while letting people move between compatible applications.

## Durable foundations

Clear specifications and independent implementations make an ecosystem more resilient.

articles.title: Privacy Beyond Transaction Content
articles.description: Timing, network behavior, and account habits can matter alongside transaction details.
articles.content:
# Privacy Beyond Transaction Content

Protecting transaction content is important, but metadata can also reveal patterns. Privacy-aware design considers what an observer can infer from timing and repeated behavior.

## Layered protection

No single feature solves every privacy problem. Clear expectations help people choose appropriate tools.

articles.title: Recovery Planning Before You Need It
articles.description: A calm backup plan is easier to create before a device is lost or damaged.
articles.content:
# Recovery Planning Before You Need It

Wallet recovery material can control funds, so it deserves deliberate handling. Keep it private, verify the process, and avoid relying on a single device.

## Practice safely

Understand the recovery flow with minimal value before depending on it.
